item.title: Self-Hosted Remote Attestation Platforms: Keylime vs CoCo vs IMA/EVM
item.description: Remote attestation is the process of cryptographically verifying that a remote system is running trusted software in a known-good state. For self-hosted infrastructure, remote attestation provides critical security assurance: before deploying workloads to a server, you can verify its firmware, bootloader, kernel, and application integrity — detecting tampering, rootkits, or unauthorized modifications.
